chapter: Chicago pioneers, community and New Orleans brotherhood
title: Mahalia Jackson's award and the Martin Luther King concert band
summary: A plaque from Mahalia Jackson honours his 42-piece band for her Martin Luther King concert at the start of union integration.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Right, well, see this has been my life. I've lived in this neighborhood, this community and things. And a lot of them -- and the awards and things, you know? Now, Mahalia Jackson, there, there's one from Mahalia Jackson up here. And that was given to me in appreciation for a concert that she had arranged for Martin Luther King. And we furnished the band for her. I got the band for her, and she -- and then, this was right at the beginning of the integration of the union, so the union gave her -- oh, let's see, what was it? I think it was a 42-piece band, and I was the conductor for it and everything. Then she gave us this award, and she gave one to Barney Pichards who was president of Local 10 at that time.
Well, do you still do a lot of community work?
